adherence.reason: The text is clearly framed and developed as a locked-room detective story.
Elias performs the investigation, but the text never clearly identifies him as a private investigator who was called in.
Julian Aris is found murdered inside the apparently locked study.
Elias repeatedly speaks his deductions aloud to an explicitly imagined or invisible audience.
The door is presented as locked from within and a key is found in the victim's pocket, but Elias later finds a duplicate key, contradicting the claim that it was the only key.
The exact phrase "the room lied before anyone else did." appears verbatim multiple times.
A flashback reveals that Elias opened a hidden wall panel and let Julian into the study three hours earlier without anticipating the murder.
The closing scene centers on Elias confessing to Inspector Miller that his unwitting use of the passage and subsequent negligence enabled the locked-room setup.
